<t3_code_instructions>
## T3 Code interaction mode: Default

Prefer making reasonable assumptions and carrying out the user's request. Ask a concise question only when a missing user decision would materially change the result. Treat this mode as active until T3 Code supplies a different interaction-mode instruction.

## T3 Code browser

When browser work was asked, `preview_*` is the browser you share with the user: `preview_status` first, then `preview_open` if no tab can be automated. Prefer snapshot locators over coordinates. Switch browsers only if the tools are absent or `preview_open` says unsupported, the user asks, or two preview calls fail on one step. Then quote the error and switch.

## T3 Code orchestration

Ordinary coding tasks need no T3 tools.

- Subagents: use your native tool when the child uses your provider, a model it offers and no settings beyond yours (Claude `Agent`, `run_in_background:false`; Codex `spawn_agent`, then wait). Use `delegate_task` for another provider's model, user-asked settings, a separate checkout (`isolation:"worktree"`), or `delegate_task` by name. A native type on another provider's model counts too. Background agent: `delegate_task`, never a background `Agent`. Workflow only when asked.
- Call `orchestrator_capabilities` once per thread, before the first `delegate_task`. Again only after an error or a user-named provider change. Settings go in `target.options`. Provider or model unavailable: say so. Never switch unasked or fall back to native tools, Workflow or CLIs. Never make a child's checkout in the shell or in `task`.
- Every new delegate review or re-check is a new `delegate_task` (brief, findings, objections), never a `t3_thread_send`. Fix small review findings yourself; start no delegate for them. When told to proceed without a delegate, or to run fewer, `task_cancel` the extras. Start no replacement.
- Follow a running delegate's `next`. Don't poll it (`task_status`, `sleep`, watchers, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup). Stop a delegate run you replace or no longer need with `task_cancel`, never `t3_thread_interrupt` on a `childThreadId`.
- As a subagent or child, do the work yourself. Start no subagents unless your task says to.

- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` make new top-level threads, only when the user asks for a new thread. "Subagent", "delegate", and "parallel" never mean one. Worktree thread: set `workspaceStrategy`. Honor a requested base. Otherwise independent work uses the default branch as `remote/branch` with `startFromOrigin:true`; with no remote, use the local default. Required unpublished commits and dependent work use their local base. Shell worktrees don't bind it, and no checkout setup in its prompt. No `workspaceStrategy`: project root, not your worktree.
- Given a thread id, `t3_thread_read` it before you answer about it. Asked to settle a thread, this one too: `t3_thread_organize`.
- Another machine: `t3_environment_links` lists linked ones. Pass its `environmentId` and that machine's `threadId` to T3 tools.
- Unlinked ("delegate this to my vps"): `t3_environment_link` with a `hint` from the user's words, never a pairing code in chat. No link tools: say to enable Settings → Labs → Linked environments.
- In your reply, mention a thread by its `link`, verbatim, never a plain title or bare id.
- A login, token, PIN, pairing code or sudo password only the user can give: call `request_secret`, not a chat ask or a handoff. Not for access you have. Sudo: if `sudo -n <cmd>` needs a password, use `delivery: "file"` and run `sudo -S -p '' <cmd> < "$file"`; the password takes stdin, so give other input as a file argument. Asked only to schedule: `schedule_task` without running its prompt.
- T3 tools may load late. Try the name once before you call it absent.

### Visuals and preview

- Answer data with a trend or comparison with a chart and show any visual the user asks for here: pass an HTML file path or inline HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. A screenshot on disk or a text description doesn't show it. Never start a server for it. Page tools write only on user request. Never use them to show results. Asked for an image to post, send or use elsewhere: a `.png` file and its path, never `html_render`.
- Never use `preview_*` unasked to verify or show your own edit. Use them when the current request asks for browser work, including recording edits, or names a page or tab. Don't repeat preview calls from an earlier turn. Public pages: web fetch or search unless browser work was asked; then preview tools only, no web fetch. Close a tab you opened before you reply, unless the user asked for it or uses it.

ACP fallback: if the T3 tools are absent and `T3_ACP_MCP_NODE` is present, call them through the terminal: `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$T3_ACP_MCP_NODE" ${T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT:+"$T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT"} acp-mcp-call orchestrator_capabilities '{}'` (`T3_ACP_MCP_ENTRYPOINT` is unset for a standalone executable). Delegate with `acp-mcp-call delegate_task '{"task":"...","target":{"providerInstanceId":"...","model":"..."},"mode":"async","clientRequestId":"..."}'`.
</t3_code_instructions>

1→---
name: poteto-mode
description: poteto's agent style for concise, detailed responses, deliberate subagents, unslopped prose, simple code, and verified work. Use for poteto, /poteto-mode, or requests to work in this style.
---

# Poteto mode

Bundled skills live at `../<name>/SKILL.md` from this file, so put this file's absolute path in every `poteto-agent` prompt.

10→## Platform Adaptation

These skills use Claude Code tool names (the `Skill` tool, the `Agent` tool, `AskUserQuestion`) and the Claude model names the `Agent` tool accepts, as each Models section lists them. On Claude Code they work as written. On Codex, read [`references/codex-tools.md`](references/codex-tools.md) for the Codex equivalent of a Claude tool, model, or skill named by these workflows. On Pi, read [`references/pi-tools.md`](references/pi-tools.md) instead. On GitHub Copilot, read [`references/copilot-tools.md`](references/copilot-tools.md) instead. On Muse, read [`references/muse-tools.md`](references/muse-tools.md) instead. On MiniMax Code, read [`references/minimax-tools.md`](references/minimax-tools.md) instead. On Antigravity, read [`references/agy-tools.md`](references/agy-tools.md) instead. On OMP, read [`references/omp-tools.md`](references/omp-tools.md) instead. On Kimi Code CLI, read [`references/kimi-tools.md`](references/kimi-tools.md) instead. On Grok Build, read [`references/grok.md`](references/grok.md) instead. On OpenCode 2, read [`references/opencode-tools.md`](references/opencode-tools.md) instead. Other runtimes can discover the same Agent Skills tree, but they must use their own tool, model, and configuration equivalents. No one of these mappings is a cross-runtime map.

Use the session's task-tracking tools for the todolist. On Claude Code these are `TaskCreate` and `TaskUpdate`, or `TodoWrite` when configured. Availability depends on the model; `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` enables them through the environment or a project's `.claude/settings.local.json` `env` block. See the [task-tool documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#task-tool-availability). If no task-tracking tool is available, keep an uncommitted `todo.md` Markdown checklist in the work dir, next to the decision trail, with the playbook steps verbatim and each `skip: <reason>` line. When several sessions share the checkout, name it `.audit/<task-slug>.todo.md`, beside that session's `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` trail, so they never write one file. In the Claude desktop app, `mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan` asks for items of about seven words. Give it that short plan, and keep this checklist as well, with the playbook steps verbatim and each `skip: <reason>` line.

## Non-negotiables

The Principles section below grounds every trigger. In your reply, name each principle that shaped a decision and the specific choice it changed. Cite only principles whose leaf SKILL.md you read this session.

20→The remaining triggers live only here:

- First message → restate the user's goal and the smallest change that meets it, then proceed. Open each subagent brief, PR `## Why`, and final report with the goal.
- Starting any agent, whether an `Agent` subagent or a background worker → the first line of its kickoff is `Read <path>/worker.md before anything else.`, with `<path>` the absolute path of this skill's folder. The operator's rules live in skills that only load from a slash command, so they reach another agent no other way. Keep the rest of the kickoff to the goal and the task, plus this file's absolute path for a `poteto-agent`.
- A fork you could settle by running something → prototype it per `playbooks/prototype.md` instead of asking.
- Code → name the data shape first. Across a function boundary → **architect**. Fan-out → **swarm**. Bakeoff → **arena**. Contested design → **interrogate**. For Bug fix only, check the [focused-fix exception](playbooks/bug-fix.md#focused-fix-exception) before **architect**.
- Prose, your reply included → **unslop**. Docs, PR descriptions, commit messages → **technical-writing**, on top of **unslop**.
- Before commit → `/deslop`. Before review → **no-comments**.
- Shipping UI / IDE / CLI → the driver skill. `run` ships with Claude Code and the model can invoke it for CLIs, TUIs, servers, and browser or Electron apps. The bundled `verify` runs only when the user types `/verify`, so for UIs use the project `verify` skill at `.claude/skills/verify/` (generate it with `/create-verification-skill`) and fall back to `run` when the repo has none.
- A number you measured → **benchmark-checklist**.
30→- PR status → the **Babysit** playbook, not the bundled **babysit** skill. Landing a green stack → the **Shipping** playbook.
- Bot review comments → judge each on its merits, per `references/bugbot-triage.md`.
- Deploying to a managed platform (Railway, Fly, Vercel, Heroku, and the like) → load that platform's skill, project-local or installed, before running its CLI, the same way Shipping step 1 resolves the forge before the first PR operation.
- A defect found mid-task → severity decides its artifact, not where it turned up. A correctness or data gap gets a tracked issue even when it surfaces while writing a closure doc; a cosmetic margin can stay in the doc.
- Long or unattended work → **show-me-your-work**.

## Principles

Read the leaf skill in full for any principle you apply. Each entry names when it applies. Each leaf is the **principle-<title>** skill, with the title in kebab case, hyphens kept and other punctuation dropped, unless the entry gives its name.

40→**Core**

- **Laziness Protocol.** Refactoring, sizing a diff, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias to deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.
- **Foundational Thinking.** Before writing logic: core types and data structures, scaffold-vs-feature sequencing, what concurrent actors share.
- **Redesign from First Principles.** Integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if it had been foundational from day one.
- **Attack the Premise.** Two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate. Write the premise down and test it directly before you write another fix that assumes it.
- **Subtract Before You Add.** Sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead weight first, then build on the simpler base.
- **Minimize Reader Load.** Reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers and hidden state, collapse one-caller wrappers, shrink mutable scope.
- **Outcome-Oriented Execution.** Planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture, don't preserve throwaway compatibility states.
- **Experience First.** Product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs. Choose user delight over implementation convenience.
50→- **Exhaust the Design Space.** A novel interaction or architectural decision with no precedent. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare before committing.
- **Build the Lever.** Any non-trivial work. Build the tool that does or proves it (codemod, script, generator), not by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer reruns.

**Architecture**

- **Model the Domain.** Writing stateful logic, or code that branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure (state machine, typed model, table or registry, reducer, boundary, the right collection) instead of scattered conditionals.
- **Boundary Discipline.** Wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Guards at system boundaries, trust internal types, keep business logic pure.
- **Type System Discipline.** Designing types or a signature in any typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand primitives, parse external data at boundaries.
- **Make Operations Idempotent.** Designing commands, lifecycle steps, or loops that run amid crashes and retries. Converge to the same end state.
- **Migrate Callers Then Delete Legacy APIs.** Introducing a new internal API while old callers exist. Migrate and delete in one wave.
60→- **Separate Before Serializing Shared State.** Concurrent actors might write the same file, branch, key, or object. Eliminate the sharing first.

**Verification**

- **Prove It Works.** After a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact, not a proxy or "it compiles".
- **Fix Root Causes.** Debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.
- **Sequence Work into Verifiable Units** (**principle-sequence-verifiable-units**). Multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a check, verify each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself.
- **Test Behavior, Not Implementation.** Writing, changing, or keeping a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.
- **Explain the Number.** Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured (a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result). Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

70→**Delegation**

- **Guard the Context Window.** Context fills up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents, keep summaries in the main thread.
- **Never Block on the Human.** Tempted to ask "should I do X?" on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct.

**Meta**

- **Encode Lessons in Structure.** You catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time. Encode it as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.

## Autonomy
80→
**Just do it.** Use any MCP tool. Reversible work and external actions (team chat, ticket updates, kicking off evals) proceed without asking.

**Always pause** for irreversible writes: force-push to shared branches, deploys, data deletion, customer messages.

**Session overrides:** "Don't stop" / "going to bed" / "run until done" / "be fully autonomous" → keep going.

**No is an acceptable answer.** Asked whether to do something, invited to add scope, or shown an approach, reply with your real judgment. Decline, push back, or say "this doesn't earn its place" when true. A recommendation is a judgment, not a validation. Agreement is not the default, candor over sycophancy.

## Subagents
90→
**Use `subagent_type: "pstack:poteto-agent"` for any subagent you spawn directly inside a playbook step.** Plugin agents register under the plugin namespace. The bare name `poteto-agent` errors. The chat that receives `/poteto-mode` runs the playbook itself. Routed workflow skills (`interrogate`, `swarm`) set their own `subagent_type`. Respect it.

**Defaults for every `Agent` call.** `run_in_background: true`, full tool access (do not pick a subagent_type that strips MCP), file pointers not inlined context, and an explicit model per role, background workers included. `/setup-pstack` writes `pstack-models.md`, whose per-role lines override the defaults below and the role models in the routed skills (`arena`, `swarm`, `interrogate`). A role with no line keeps its default. A line of `inherit-parent` or `auto` runs the role on the parent model, so omit `model` on the `Agent` call. `poteto-agent` sets no model of its own, so it then runs on the parent model. Each code playbook reads its own line (`feature, refactoring`, `bug-fix`, `perf-issue`, or `hillclimb`), prose and judgment read `judgment and prose`, and trivial mechanical edits read `swarm workers`.

Role defaults for code, prose, judgment, trivial mechanical edits, and the diverse review and design panels are in [Models](#models).

**The `strongest judgment` model is an exception.** It runs outside a panel only when the user named it for this task or two xhigh runs of the same brief on the task's own role model failed their check. Say which. Difficulty alone never qualifies.

**Match the model to the job.** Start from the role's line or default, keep its family, and set the level the job needs. The role's `@level`, or the sheet's `default effort` line, sets its starting level, and `session` starts from the session's level. Panel seats keep their listed level. Raise any other role one step, up to xhigh, for the hardest or subtlest work, lower it one step for judgment, and two or more steps for routine work. No role runs above xhigh unless the sheet sets a higher level on the role's line or the `default effort` line. Verification always runs on the `swarm workers` model (default in the **swarm** skill's Models section). If the `Agent` tool rejects a slug, never pass it again. Fall back to the role's line or default, then the calling skill's fallback, then the closest valid slug of the same family, then omit `model`. Say so.
100→
You own every subagent's work. Review the diff and write your own summary. A second opinion is the same prompt on a model from another family.

**Fresh subagents by default.** Give a fix round, a follow-up, a retry, or the next queue item to a fresh subagent with the original brief, every later directive, and the prior agent's report and branch. Resume an existing subagent only when the work needs state that lives in it and is costly to move: its checkout, its uncommitted changes, or a process it still runs. **Stop the abandoned agent first, and confirm it stopped.** In the agent listing `completed` means the completion was *notified*, not that the process exited: an agent with live background children reports completed and then resumes. Only an explicit stop ends it, and the stop tool may be deferred, so load it before you need it. The tell that one is still running is a claim about the working tree that `git status` contradicts.

**A review gate stays closed when no independent reviewer can run.** An agent limit, subagent dispatch turned off, or a skills-only install can leave a required review with no reviewer. Keep the results of reviewers already dispatched. As the one exception to fresh subagents, reuse a finished reviewer only through the runtime's own follow-up action, only if it did not write the change, and only with the full current brief and head revision. A reused reviewer counts once. Never count your own review, passing tests, or CI as the independent verdict. Record `BLOCKED: independent review` in the todolist, keep merge-ready and shipping closed, and report which reviewers ran and which are missing. Work that doesn't depend on the review continues. A fan-out skill run only to explore may fall back to one labelled sequential pass.

## Writing the reply

Write short declarative sentences with no long dash and no colon as a connector. Lead with what changes for the user. Give each claim its evidence or a label (measured, inferred, or guess). Never hand the human a check you could run. Keep every item the playbook's reply names, each rendered as prose, with no section headers.
110→
## Playbooks

This appears to be a continuation of prior work. The session pickup playbook may apply.

I will read the session pickup playbook and grok.md to assess the current state. I will then continue the Release 3 issue work. The main agent will investigate and decide scope. Substantial implementation will be delegated.

I will check the worktrees, GitHub issues 297, 301, and 296, and any existing research notes and decision maps. The session pickup playbook should be read first, with its steps copied into the todolist tool.

1→### Session pickup

**You own the resume point. Read the prior trail, don't redo it.**

1. Read the project checkpoint first using [Resume storage](../references/resume-storage.md). A successful read gives the note and artifacts without requiring a path from the previous session. If the pointer is missing, locate the prior trail through a local transcript under Claude Code's per-project transcripts directory at `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl` (`node <plugin>/skills/reflect/scripts/claude-project-dir.mjs` prints this session's directory, which holds the earlier sessions that started in the same directory. For one that started elsewhere, pass its start directory: `node <plugin>/skills/reflect/scripts/claude-project-dir.mjs "<start directory>"`. Do not glob across other directories under `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects/`, that crosses workspace boundaries and reads private chats from unrelated projects), a cloud-agent URL, or a pushed branch. An unavailable or incomplete checkpoint needs diagnosis rather than a silent fallback. For transcript fallback, read the metadata overview and last messages first, then scan back for the decision points. Parse a long transcript in a subagent and keep the reduced timeline in the main thread (the **principle-guard-the-context-window** skill). Pick each subagent's reasoning level for the job, per the Subagents section.
2. Reconstruct operational state. The branch and worktree, what already landed (`git log`, `git diff` against the base), the open todos, the decisions made. Use the prior trail to recover progress. For claims about human rulings, find the person's original attributable words when the exact scope matters, with a source pointer and the speaker. An agent summary is not the original ruling, and copies of one summary in several notes are one evidence chain.
3. Diff done vs pending. Compare what shipped against what was planned, name the resume point, do not re-run the prior repro or redo completed work. Recheck claims that affect the remaining work without repeating completed investigations. Read artifacts linked by the resume note, including requested questions or checklists.
4. Verify the inherited claims against the original goal on the real artifact (the **principle-prove-it-works** skill). A passing prior self-report is not the proof.
5. Route the remaining work to the matching playbook and pick the verdict: continue the execution, ship a finished recommendation, ratify or override a prior conclusion, or postmortem a failed run. The pickup playbook ends here. The routed playbook owns the rest.
10→

Do not glob across other directories under `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/projects/`, that crosses workspace boundaries and reads private chats from unrelated projects), a cloud-agent URL, or a pushed branch. An unavailable or incomplete checkpoint needs diagnosis rather than a silent fallback. For transcript fallback, read the metadata overview and last messages first, then scan back for the decision points. Parse a long transcript in a subagent and keep the reduced timeline in the main thread (the **principle-guard-the-context-window** skill). An agent summary is not the original ruling, and copies of one summary in several notes are one evidence chain.

Recheck claims that affect the remaining work without repeating completed investigations. Read artifacts linked by the resume note, including requested questions or checklists.

1→# Grok Build tool mapping for pstack

Grok Build loads the pstack plugin's skills. It does not translate Claude Code tool names in those skills. Use the tools the session exposes; availability and permissions can differ.

## Tool actions

| pstack / Claude action | Grok Build equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| Read (`Read`) | `read_file` with `target_file` set to the path in the session's skills list |
10→| Write (`Write`) / edit (`Edit`) | `write` / `search_replace` |
| Shell (`Bash`) | `run_terminal_command` |
| Search (`Grep` / `Glob`) | `grep` / `list_dir` |
| Web (`WebSearch` / `WebFetch`) | `web_search` / `run_terminal_command` with `curl` |
| Skill (`Skill`) | Read the path from the session's skills list with `read_file`; `/poteto-mode` also expands the skill |
| Subagent (`Agent` / `Task`) | `spawn_subagent` with `prompt` and `description`; `run_in_background` defaults to `true`; use `isolation: "worktree"` where needed |
| Wait for a subagent (`TaskOutput`) | `get_command_or_subagent_output` with its task ID |
| Send to a subagent (`SendMessage`) | `send_subagent_message`, off by default; `GROK_ACTIVE_AGENT_MESSAGES` or `[features] active_agent_messages` enables it. Without the tool, do not claim to have sent an update |
| Stop a subagent (`TaskStop`) | `kill_command_or_subagent` |
| Tasks (`TaskCreate` / `TaskUpdate` / `TodoWrite`) | `todo_write` |
20→| Questions (`AskUserQuestion`) | `ask_user_question` |
| MCP (`mcp__<server>__<tool>`) | `search_tool`, then `use_tool` |
| Wake-up (`ScheduleWakeup`) | For user-authorized recurring work, `scheduler_create` schedules a background subagent while the session is open; `scheduler_list` and `scheduler_delete` inspect or remove it. It is not a one-shot wake-up. |
| Claude transcript search | Grok stores sessions under `${GROK_HOME:-~/.grok}/sessions`; inspect the relevant session there rather than Claude's projects directory |

Grok does not inject the Claude SessionStart hook output. The Grok-only routing skill asks the model to read poteto-mode through its description; this is a model-followed hint, not guaranteed injection. The pstack `session hook: off` setting does not suppress it. Disable the plugin to remove the hint and its other skills.

## Subagent policy

poteto-mode's Subagents section dispatches `subagent_type: "pstack:poteto-agent"`, and other skills name `general-purpose`. The Grok build ships skills and no agent definitions.
30→
- For `pstack:poteto-agent` or `general-purpose`, omit `subagent_type`. Grok cannot select a built-in type by name and runs an omitted type as `general-purpose`.
- Put the absolute path of `poteto-mode`'s `SKILL.md` in every brief that stands in for `pstack:poteto-agent`, as poteto-mode asks.

## Model names

Skills name Claude Code model aliases in their Models sections. Grok Build's available models depend on the user's configuration; do not pass a Claude alias as a Grok model.

- The model sheet is `${GROK_HOME:-~/.grok}/pstack-models.md`. Before a skill that needs a role model (`arena`, `interrogate`, `no-comments`, `poteto-mode`, `swarm`, `thermos`), read it. With no sheet, use the runtime default; run `setup-pstack` only when the user asks to configure roles.
- The `spawn_subagent` tool says to omit `model` unless the user explicitly requests one. It has no effort parameter; when it cannot apply a sheet choice, report that limitation instead of claiming model diversity.
40→- Roles that default to the worker model (`feature, refactoring`): the worker model the user chose.
- Roles that default to the strongest model (`strongest judgment`): the strongest model the user chose.
- Diverse-model panels (`arena`, `interrogate`) require distinct models. Report when the available dispatch cannot provide that diversity.

`/setup-pstack` writes the sheet. Choose only models the session exposes.

## Per-skill notes

| Skill | On Grok Build |
| --- | --- |
50→| `why` | List MCP servers with `search_tool`, not from Claude Code's MCP files. |

The `resume.mjs` command under `skills/poteto-mode/scripts/` resolves the project's Git common directory and stores checkpoints under its `pstack/resume/` directory. `latest.json` points to the latest complete checkpoint and records the worktree, branch, timestamp, note, and requested artifacts with content hashes.

Claude Code, Codex, and other runtimes use this same command and location. Runtime-specific home directories and transcript encodings do not affect lookup. Git worktrees of the same repository share the locator, and Git excludes its contents from commits. This requires a local Git checkout whose common directory survives the interruption. It does not survive deleting or recloning the repository; transfer the complete checkpoint to durable storage before that happens and give the resumed session its locator.

## Write a checkpoint

1. Run `node <scripts>/resume.mjs begin --project <worktree>` to allocate a new checkpoint directory. Write `resume.md` there with intent, verified progress, current state, and next steps.
10→2. Save requested artifacts in that directory and link them from the note. Reuse existing artifacts in the project when their location survives the anticipated interruption. Do not make competing copies. For a worktree that will be removed, place the requested material in the common checkpoint store instead. Check exact wording, completeness, and order where required.
3. Publish with `node <scripts>/resume.mjs publish --project <worktree> --note <resume.md> --artifact <file> ...`. Register every local note link as an artifact, including existing project files. Link each local file with an inline Markdown link whose destination is the path, written bare or as `<path>`, with no square brackets in the link text and no title after the path. Reference-style links are not read. The path is relative to the note or absolute, and it is percent-decoded, so write a literal `%` as `%25`. Wrap a path that contains spaces or parentheses in angle brackets, or percent-encode it. Links inside code spans and fenced code blocks are ignored. Each rejected link reports this rule. The command verifies file ownership, links, and contents before atomically replacing `latest.json`. A failed publication must not be treated as a ready checkpoint.
4. Run `node <scripts>/resume.mjs read --project <worktree>` and open its note and artifacts. Treat published checkpoint files as immutable. Use a new checkpoint directory for a later pause. If an existing project artifact changes, pickup reports that difference rather than silently treating it as the saved material.

`begin` separates concurrent writers' files. Publishing replaces one shared latest pointer atomically; the last complete publication wins. Keep the returned checkpoint paths when multiple tasks must remain separately resumable. The pointer is a locator, not a task scheduler or execution lock.

## Read a checkpoint

Session pickup starts with `node <scripts>/resume.mjs read --project <worktree>` using only the project directory. Exit 0 with `kind: checkpoint` provides the saved note and all registered artifacts. Open them before searching transcripts. The command validates hashes and links again, including reuse of project artifacts.

20→Exit 2 with `kind: missing` means there is no pointer, so use the transcript, cloud URL, or branch fallback. Exit 1 with `kind: unavailable` means a checkpoint is malformed, unreadable, changed, or incomplete. Diagnose that concrete gap; do not silently ignore the checkpoint or claim the material was never saved. None of these commands causes a running task to pause.

## Destination

Release 3 "Reach and close the loop" is ready to build for small Teams first: Channel-agnostic delivery across Email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams; Action follow-up Questions and Comment theme deep-dives; Core + Rotating Questions; and a privacy-enforced remote MCP server. Every hard-to-reverse decision is recorded in ADRs (`docs/adr/`), `SPEC.md §8` is updated to reflect the re-sequencing, `GLOSSARY.md` carries any new terms, and R3 is split into implementation-sized issues under a "Release 3: implementation" tracking issue.

## Notes

- Domain: `SPEC.md` is the source, `GLOSSARY.md` the vocabulary, ADRs 0001–0026 bind. Use glossary terms in every ticket (Pulse, Round, Person, Lead, Submission, Answer, Minimum group size, Comment theme, Discussion guide, Action, Review window, Channel, Distribution, Redaction).
- Planning only. No production code. Throwaway spikes are allowed as `prototype` or `task` tickets when a decision depends on one.
- Trust before features (`SPEC.md §3.1`): when a choice trades anonymity for convenience, anonymity wins. Anything sent to a third party is a new data flow and must be stated plainly to members.
- Cloudflare-only runtime (`SPEC.md §6`): everything runs on Cloudflare Workers + Durable Objects + D1. No long-running Node container or third-party cloud relay (ruling out `CopilotKit/channels-sdk` + CopilotKit Intelligence).

## Decisions so far

- **Small Teams first (product owner, 2026-11-20):** Re-sequence `SPEC.md §8` to ship small-Team habit and loop-closing features ahead of enterprise Organizations (SCIM, nested Teams, cross-Team comparisons, Confidential mode).
- **Channel-agnostic delivery — Slack + Microsoft Teams + Email (product owner, 2026-11-20):** Use a serverless, Cloudflare Workers-compatible multi-channel layer (evaluating `vercel/chat` vs thin Effect adapters) behind a domain `ChannelSender` port, starting with Slack and Microsoft Teams plus Email as the built-in fallback. Zero-Leakage Handoff: chat Channels deliver Invitations (with 1-tap first-Question links), Reminders, and Shared Results summaries, while Answers still confirm on `answer.html` through the zero-observability `SubmissionWorker` (preserving ADR 0005).
- **Closing the loop & anti-fatigue (product owner, 2026-11-20):** Pull up Action follow-up Questions, one-click Comment theme deep-dive Questions (privacy-safe alternative to server-linked 1:1 anonymous chat), and Core + Rotating Questions into Release 3.
- **Remote MCP server privacy default (product owner, 2026-11-20):** Raw redacted comments are **off by default** over MCP (default exposes scores, Comment themes, Actions, Notes, and Lead-only Discussion guide), with an opt-in Organization setting for raw redacted comments. Organization admins still see no Results (ADR 0003).

## Not yet specified

- **Legal text for the new data flows.** Release 3 slices must describe the Slack, Microsoft Teams and MCP data flows on the privacy page and in legal text, but the public legal pages and the sub-processor register do not exist yet ([GDPR: Public legal pages (Privacy Notice, Terms, DPA, Sub-processors) and in-app transparency](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/305)). Whether Slack and Microsoft count as SurveyBeat sub-processors or as the customer's own tools, and which ticket owns that text, waits on the Channel delivery design.
- **Data subject rights for new personal data.** Chat identity links (email ↔ chat user), workspace installations and MCP OAuth grants are new personal data. Export and erasure ([GDPR: Right of Access and Portability — personal data export (Art. 15, Art. 20)](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/306), [GDPR: Right to Erasure — true personal data deletion for People (Art. 17)](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/307)) must cover them once their storage is decided.
- **Teams fallback shape.** If research finds that Microsoft Teams Safe Links drops the URL fragment, the "Open check-in"-only Teams Invitation may need its own UX decision.

## Out of scope

- Enterprise Organizations release (deferred to Release 4): Enterprise SSO / SCIM Directory Sync, nested Teams and subtraction-safe roll-ups, standard Questions and cross-Team comparison, Confidential mode, Audit log, CSV/PDF exports.
- Issue tracker sync for Actions (Linear / Jira / GitHub Issues) and public REST API / webhooks.
- In-chat Answer submission that routes Answers through Slack/Teams webhooks or `MainWorker` (revisit only via a dedicated ADR if teams ask for it).

## Review of the child tickets (2026-11-20)

The product owner accepted every recommendation from the review. Each ticket's body holds its part:

- #300 and #302 are now blocked by #299.
- Chat Invitations use plain links only and turn link previews off; the message is edited to remove answer links once the member answers or the Round closes (#298).
- Results summaries post only once the Result is shared, without comments, counts or the Discussion guide (#298).
- MCP serves Leads only, checks that the Person is active and not banned, and turning on raw comments adds a line to the answer page's anonymity statement (#301, #302).
- Round order: core, then rotating, then One-Round Questions, so Question 1 stays a rating (#299, #300).
- Release 4 = Enterprise Organizations, Release 5 = Public API, webhooks, "Ask your results", issue-tracker sync. Slack ships before Teams within Release 3. "Live Redaction Preview" is dropped (#296).



=== 295 last comments ===
---
The Release 3 scope decision from #296 is in the pull request for `t3/r3-296-release-order`: Release 3 is Reach and close the loop, Release 4 is Enterprise Organizations, Release 5 is the public API and webhooks. Live Redaction Preview stays out.

1→# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --json number,title,body,labels,comments`.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
10→- **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**: `gh issue create --parent <parent> ...`, or `gh issue edit <parent> --add-sub-issue <child>` afterwards (`gh` 2.94+). Older `gh`: `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<parent>/sub_issues -F sub_issue_id=<child-db-id>` (database id, as in **Blocking** below). Without sub-issues, put `Part of #<parent>` at the top of the child body.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh issue create --blocked-by <n>,<n> ...` or `gh issue edit <child> --add-blocked-by <blocker>` (`gh` 2.94+). Older `gh`: `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Count open blockers**: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only; 0 means startable). `gh issue view <n> --json blockedBy` also lists closed blockers, so filter it: `--jq '[.blockedBy.nodes[] | select(.state == "OPEN")] | length'`.
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: post the explanation with `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`, then `gh issue close <number>`. On an already-closed issue, `gh issue close --comment` drops the comment and still exits 0.

Infer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

File issues only into the user's own repo. Never file into `mattpocock/skills` (the repo these skills come from) unless the user owns it. In a fork, `gh` can default to the upstream parent, so before the first `gh issue create` of a session, check the target with `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner` and confirm it with the user if it is not their repo.
20→
## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number>`, then `gh pr view <number> --comments` (off a TTY, `--comments` prints only the comments, not the body), and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh api --paginate 'repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls?state=open' --jq '.[] | select(.author_association | IN("OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR") | not) | {number, title, author: .user.login, author_association, labels: [.labels[].name]}'`.
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.
30→
GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Read it as in **Read an issue** above.
40→
## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (see **Make an issue a sub-issue of a parent**). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: see **Blocking** under Conventions.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (see **Count open blockers**, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.
50→- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

content.text:
# Can vercel/chat run SurveyBeat's Slack and Microsoft Teams Channels?

Research for issue #297 (map #295, Release 3). Researched 2026-11-20 against `chat`, `@chat-adapter/slack` and `@chat-adapter/teams` **4.45.0** (published 2026-11-13). This note changes no code, adds no dependency and edits neither `SPEC.md` nor any ADR. The Channel ADR (numbers 0027+) takes its constraints from §4.

Claims marked *(secondary)* come from a forum or Q&A thread, not from vendor documentation. Claims marked *(measured)* come from the throwaway probes described in §2.1, which are not committed.

## 1. Recommendation

**Use thin custom Effect adapters for Slack and Microsoft Teams behind the domain `ChannelSender` port. Do not adopt the `Chat` runtime, its `StateAdapter`, or the full `@chat-adapter/*` packages.**

The `Chat` runtime is built for conversational bots (threads, subscriptions, locks, message dedupe), and R3's Channel work is outbound-first plus one slash command. The full adapters do run in workerd (*measured*), but the Teams adapter alone adds about 897 KiB gzip and spent 1.8 s of active startup CPU in the one local profile that finished, against a 1 s Worker startup limit; the `Chat` runtime also needs a `StateAdapter` that SurveyBeat has no Cloudflare-native, Organization-isolated implementation of.

What to build, in order:

1. **Slack first**, as #295 sequences it. About five endpoints are needed: signature verification (Web Crypto HMAC), `oauth.v2.access`, `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`/`chat.delete`, and `users.lookupByEmail`. All are plain `fetch` calls validated with Effect Schema at the boundary.
2. **Teams second, behind a tenancy spike** (§3.6). The Azure Bot tenancy rules changed in 2025 and a single-tenant bot may not reach other customers' tenants. This is the largest unresolved risk in R3.
3. **No external store, no `StateAdapter`.** Everything an outbound-first Channel needs (installation token, Person-to-Channel binding, sent-message id for later edits) is Organization state and belongs in the Organization Durable Object beside the existing `SendStore`. Redis would break SPEC §6; the Durable Object SQLite `StateAdapter` that exists today ships in Cloudflare's `agents` package, not in `vercel/chat` (§3.3), and is not worth taking on for a surface this narrow.
4. **Treat `@chat-adapter/{slack,teams}` as reference and test vectors**, not as a dependency. Their stateless subpath modules (`/webhook`, `/api`, `/blocks`, `/cards`) are small, MIT, `fetch`-based and run in workerd with 13.1 KiB gzip (*measured*). Our code is smaller than the cost of tracking a package that shipped seven minor releases between 2026-08-14 and 2026-11-13. If the Channel ADR prefers to reuse them, it must name the package and pin an exact version. AGENTS.md requires that naming when a new Ratstack template package is added; the closer rule here is ADR 0008, which pins unstable dependencies.

**Revisit this if** a later release wants in-chat conversation (threads, "reply to answer", streaming). Then `chat` plus Cloudflare's `agents/chat-sdk` state adapter is the route to evaluate, and #295's exclusion of in-chat Answer submission would need its own ADR.

## 2. Answers to the issue's questions

| Question | Answer | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does `vercel/chat` run on Workers with Alchemy and Effect 4.1.x (`nodejs_compat`)? | Yes, mechanically. `wrangler deploy --dry-run` bundles Slack, Teams and both together, and local workerd serves and rejects bad signatures. It is promise-based, so every call is wrapped in `Effect.tryPromise`. No Alchemy-specific obstacle was found, but I did not deploy through Alchemy. | §2.1, *measured* |
| Workerd compatibility and footprint? | Slack full: 277 KiB gz. Teams full: 897 KiB gz, 1.8 s active startup in the one local profile that finished (two others timed out at 10 s). Both: 996 KiB gz. Stateless subpaths: 13 KiB gz. Worker size limit is 64 MiB, so **startup time, not size, is the limiter.** | §2.1, *measured* |
| Signature verification and stateless handling in `MainWorker`? | Slack: HMAC-SHA256 with Web Crypto, 5-minute skew, no state. Teams: Microsoft's JWT check, which the stateless subpath does **not** implement; we write it. | §3.2 |
| Does it need Redis or another external store? | The `Chat` constructor requires a `StateAdapter`; official ones are Redis, ioredis, Postgres, memory. Redis and Postgres are third-party stores and break SPEC §6. A DO SQLite `StateAdapter` exists but is Cloudflare's `agents/chat-sdk`, not part of `vercel/chat`. With thin adapters, **no `StateAdapter` is required.** | §3.3 |
| Card fidelity? | Slack Block Kit and Teams Adaptive Cards both carry what R3 needs: rating links, a Reminder, a Result summary, and later edits. Plain-link Invitations are possible on both. | §3.4 |
| Slack app and Teams bot registration and per-Organization OAuth install? | Slack: standard distributed app plus OAuth v2 install per workspace. Teams: Entra app plus Azure Bot plus Teams app package; per-tenant admin install; tenancy model unresolved. | §3.5, §3.6 |
| Teams proactive messages, and where does the conversation reference live? | Needs the bot installed in the Person's personal scope, plus tenant id, user id and service URL. Store the per-Person reference in the **Organization Durable Object**; D1 holds only the tenant-to-Organization routing row. | §3.6 |
| Safe Links and the fragment `#t=…&v=…`? | **Not tested.** Microsoft documents that Teams links are checked at click time and not rewritten, and says nothing about fragments. Teams is gated on the fragment surviving. Whether Microsoft receives it is a separate question a `location.hash` check cannot answer. | §3.7 |
| Slack plain links and `block_actions`? | Slack documents `block_actions` as the payload for Block Kit interactive components, and a URL button still sends one. Plain `<url\|text>` links in message text are not interactive components. **Slack does not state "plain links send nothing" in so many words;** the conclusion follows from its payload list and is a one-click live check. | §3.8 |

### 2.1 How the footprint was measured

In a scratch directory outside the repository I installed the four 4.45.0 packages (plus `@chat-adapter/state-memory`) and wrote five tiny Worker entries. Each used `compatibility_date = 2026-11-01` and `nodejs_compat`, wrangler 4.165.0, Node 26.

| Entry | `wrangler deploy --dry-run` | Local `wrangler check startup`, active CPU |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stateless subpaths only (`slack/webhook`, `slack/api`, `slack/blocks`, `teams/api`, `teams/cards`, `teams/webhook`) | 56.5 KiB / **13.1 KiB gz** | 19 / 99 / 59 ms |
| `Chat` + Slack adapter + memory state | 1,324 KiB / **277 KiB gz** | 232 / 93 / 63 ms |
| `Chat` + Teams adapter + memory state | 4,839 KiB / **897 KiB gz** | 1,795 ms; the other two runs timed out at 10 s |
| `Chat` + Slack + Teams + memory state | 5,332 KiB / **996 KiB gz** | 952 / 449 / 700 ms |
| For scale: Effect HttpApi Worker (`docs/research/effect-on-workers.md`) | about 86 KiB gz | 54–61 ms |

Caveats that matter:

- Startup numbers are **local workerd on a shared, noisy machine**, so they are indicative only. Cloudflare warns that production CPUs differ, and `docs/research/effect-on-workers.md` makes the same point. The Worker startup limit is 1 s ([Workers limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/)). A Teams adapter that sometimes needs more than a second locally is not a safe thing to load into `MainWorker`.
- The Worker size limit on both plans is 64 MiB (same page), so 1 MiB gzip is not a size problem. It is a startup-parse and review-surface problem.
- Behaviour check in local workerd: `bot.webhooks.slack` returned `401 Invalid signature` for a bad signature, and `bot.webhooks.teams` returned `401` for a missing `Authorization` header. That proves the modules load and the rejection path works. **It does not prove a valid inbound activity or an outbound send**, which need real Slack and Azure credentials.
- Why the Teams adapter is so heavy: its dependencies are `@microsoft/teams.apps` (needs Node ≥ 22.12; depends on `express`, `axios`, `jsonwebtoken`, `jwks-rsa`, `@azure/msal-node`, `@microsoft/signalr`, `reflect-metadata`) plus `teams.api`, `teams.cards`, `teams.graph` and `teams.graph-endpoints` ([npm metadata](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/teams.apps)). Slack's full adapter pulls `@slack/web-api` and `@slack/socket-mode`.

## 3. Evidence

### 3.1 What `vercel/chat` is

- Chat SDK is a TypeScript bot framework: a `Chat` instance holds platform adapters and one state adapter; handlers such as `bot.onNewMention` and `onSubscribedMessage` run for events from every adapter, and each adapter exposes `bot.webhooks.<name>` ([Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/chat-sdk/adapters)). Repository: [vercel/chat](https://github.com/vercel/chat), MIT.
- The state adapter "share[s] subscriptions, locks, and cached data across requests" (same page). Core `Chat` calls it on every inbound message: `setIfNotExists` for `dedupe:<adapter>:<messageId>` and `acquireLock` per thread (read in `chat@4.45.0` `dist/index.js`).
- Release cadence is fast: 4.38.0 on 2026-08-14 to 4.45.0 on 2026-11-13. The docs warn that protected members of official adapters "can change in minor releases, so pin the adapter version" ([Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/chat-sdk/adapters)).
- The repo already pins Effect and Alchemy together because both are unstable or beta (ADR 0008). A third fast-moving dependency in the send path is a cost, not a saving, for a surface of about five calls per platform.

### 3.2 Webhook verification and stateless handling in `MainWorker`

**Slack.** Requests carry `x-slack-request-timestamp` and `x-slack-signature`; the adapter verifies `v0=` + HMAC-SHA256 over `v0:<timestamp>:<body>` with `crypto.subtle`, and rejects a timestamp more than 300 s off (`@chat-adapter/slack@4.45.0`, `dist/chunk-KYABMAGK.js`). This is stateless an

... (output truncated) ...

where URLs are rewritten to `*.safelinks.protection.outlook.com` (the existing note `docs/research/email-link-scanners.md`).
- The Built-in protection preset applies Safe Links protection in Teams to every recipient in a tenant with at least one Defender for Office 365 licence.
- "The intermediary page that does Safe Links validation redirects to the target page", which the page mentions when explaining why `SameSite=Strict` cookies may fail after opening a link from Teams.

What it does not say: whether the validation request includes the fragment, whether the intermediary redirect keeps it, or whether links inside a bot's Adaptive Card are treated like links in a typed message. A browser inherits the original fragment across an HTTP 3xx redirect when the `Location` header carries none (RFC 9110 §10.2.2), but the page does not say the intermediary uses a 3xx rather than a script redirect.

Two separate risks follow:

1. **The fragment is lost.** `#t=…` and `&v=…` share one fragment, so the likely failure is that both are lost, not just `&v=`. The issue's fallback ("Open check-in only") still needs the token. If the fragment does not survive, the Teams Invitation has no anonymous-safe handoff to `answer.html`. The Channel ADR must treat that as **blocking for Teams**, not as a degraded mode.
2. **The fragment reaches Microsoft.** If the click-time check sends the full URL to Microsoft's service, the Invitation token (ADR 0005 keeps it in the fragment so that no scanner or log ever sees it) is exposed to a third party. Email already has the same unknown; this note adds no evidence either way.

Test plan for the spike: in a Defender-licensed test tenant with Teams protection on, post a bot Adaptive Card whose link is `https://<preview-stage>/a#t=TEST&v=3`; click it from desktop, web and mobile; read `location.hash` on the answer page (it can log nothing but its own hash to the console for the test). That shows whether the fragment survived. It does not show whether Microsoft received it. Then repeat with the protection setting off as a control; and repeat with the link in a `TextBlock` and in `Action.OpenUrl`. Expected cost: half a day plus a tenant.

### 3.8 Slack: plain links and `block_actions`

- The Slack interaction docs list `block_actions` as the payload for a "Block Kit interactive component", alongside shortcuts, `view_submission` and `view_closed` ([handling user interaction](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/)).
- A button that has a `url` is still an interactive component: "If you're using url, you'll still receive an interaction payload and will need to send an acknowledgement response" ([button element](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/block-elements/button-element/)). **So link buttons do send `block_actions` to our Request URL; plain links do not need to be buttons.** The Chat SDK's `link-button` renders as a `button` with `url` and an `action_id` (`@chat-adapter/slack` `blocks.js`), so it would trigger this; its plain `link` element renders as a `section` with `<url|label>`, which is not an interactive component. That a click sends nothing is the same inference from the payload list, not a sentence Slack publishes.
- The Events API `link_shared` event is sent "when a link — matching the registered URL domain your app is setup to track — is posted", not when it is clicked; it also requires a subscription and a registered domain, and apps do not receive it for their own messages ([link_shared](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/link_shared/)). SurveyBeat should register no unfurl domain and subscribe to no `link_shared`.
- **What is not stated.** Slack does not publish a sentence of the form "clicking a plain link sends nothing to the app". The conclusion rests on the payload list above. Unfurling is a separate matter: with `unfurl_links` left on, Slack's servers may fetch the URL (they send no fragment); set `unfurl_links` and `unfurl_media` to false as #295 requires. A live check costs a few minutes: post a message with five plain links to a dev workspace, subscribe the Request URL to a request log, click each, and confirm zero requests.

## 4. Constraints the Channel ADR must keep

1. **Port, not product.** `ChannelSender` stays in `packages/domain` with no Slack, Teams or Cloudflare imports; Slack and Teams senders live in `packages/cloudflare` (boundary rules, ADR 0008). The domain port speaks Invitation, Reminder and Result summary, not "message" or "thread".
2. **No third-party store, no `Chat` runtime in `MainWorker`.** If a later ADR adopts `chat`, it must also name the `StateAdapter` and show it is Cloudflare-only (the Cloudflare `agents` adapter, or one we write over the Organization Durable Object).
3. **Plain links only, previews off.** No Block Kit buttons (including `url` buttons) and no Adaptive Card `Action.Submit`/`Action.Execute`. Slack: `unfurl_links:false`, `unfurl_media:false`, no `link_shared` subscription. Teams: `Action.OpenUrl` or markdown links only. The intent is that no Channel click event carries a Person and a time (ADR 0005, ADR 0007). For Slack, "a plain link sends nothing" is inferred from the payload list until the live check in §3.8 runs. SPEC §5.1 still says that in Slack and Teams the message has interactive buttons and, where the platform allows it, a modal, and §5.7 says members can answer from the messages. #295 and this constraint require plain links and no buttons. The Channel ADR, or a SPEC edit in the same change, has to reconcile that instead of leaving the contradiction silent.

10. **Slack before Teams, Teams behind two spikes:** the tenancy spike (§3.6) and the Safe Links spike (§3.7). Slash command design for Teams (bot command or message extension) is a separate item.
11. **Edits remove links.** Both platforms support editing a sent message by stored id, which #298 relies on; the binding must therefore keep the Slack `channel` + `ts` and the Teams `conversationId` + `activityId` for each send.
12. **One workspace, one Organization.** Reject installing a Slack workspace or Teams tenant that is already bound to another Organization.

- **Teams Safe Links and the fragment.** No tenant, no Defender licence. Only the documentation in §3.7 was read.
- **Teams tenancy.** Whether one single-tenant Azure Bot can send proactive messages into other customers' tenants. Microsoft documentation does not answer it; the evidence is two Q&A threads *(secondary)*.
- **Valid-path behaviour of any adapter.** No Slack workspace or Azure Bot was available. I verified bundling, loading and the 401 rejection paths in local workerd, not a verified inbound event or an outbound `postMessage`/`createConversation`.
- **Alchemy deployment.** I used `wrangler` for bundling and local workerd. I did not deploy any of these through Alchemy or run them inside the repository's `MainWorker`.

- **Teams:** the per-card action limit; whether `Action.OpenUrl` triggers any bot activity; the Graph permission names needed to install the app proactively for a Person; and the single-tenant variants of the inbound JWT issuer and metadata.

# Can vercel/chat run SurveyBeat's Slack and Microsoft Teams Channels?

Research for issue #297 (map #295, Release 3). Researched 2026-11-20 against `chat`, `@chat-adapter/slack` and `@chat-adapter/teams` **4.45.0** (published 2026-11-13). This note changes no code, adds no dependency and edits neither `SPEC.md` nor any ADR. The Channel ADR (numbers 0027+) takes its constraints from §4.

Claims marked *(secondary)* come from a forum or Q&A thread, not from vendor documentation. Claims marked *(measured)* come from the throwaway probes described in §2.1, which are not committed.

## 1. Recommendation

**Use thin custom Effect adapters for Slack and Microsoft Teams behind the domain `ChannelSender` port. Do not adopt the `Chat` runtime, its `StateAdapter`, or the full `@chat-adapter/*` packages.**

The `Chat` runtime is built for conversational bots (threads, subscriptions, locks, message dedupe), and R3's Channel work is outbound-first plus one slash command. The full adapters do run in workerd (*measured*), but the Teams adapter alone adds about 897 KiB gzip and spent 1.8 s of active startup CPU in the one local profile that finished, against a 1 s Worker startup limit; the `Chat` runtime also needs a `StateAdapter` that SurveyBeat has no Cloudflare-native, Organization-isolated implementation of.

What to build, in order:

1. **Slack first**, as #295 sequences it. About five endpoints are needed: signature verification (Web Crypto HMAC), `oauth.v2.access`, `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`/`chat.delete`, and `users.lookupByEmail`. All are plain `fetch` calls validated with Effect Schema at the boundary.
2. **Teams second, behind a tenancy spike** (§3.6). The Azure Bot tenancy rules changed in 2025 and a single-tenant bot may not reach other customers' tenants. This is the largest unresolved risk in R3.
3. **No external store, no `StateAdapter`.** Everything an outbound-first Channel needs (installation token, Person-to-Channel binding, sent-message id for later edits) is Organization state and belongs in the Organization Durable Object beside the existing `SendStore`. Redis would break SPEC §6; the Durable Object SQLite `StateAdapter` that exists today ships in Cloudflare's `agents` package, not in `vercel/chat` (§3.3), and is not worth taking on for a surface this narrow.
4. **Treat `@chat-adapter/{slack,teams}` as reference and test vectors**, not as a dependency. Their stateless subpath modules (`/webhook`, `/api`, `/blocks`, `/cards`) are small, MIT, `fetch`-based and run in workerd with 13.1 KiB gzip (*measured*). Our code is smaller than the cost of tracking a package that shipped seven minor releases between 2026-08-14 and 2026-11-13. If the Channel ADR prefers to reuse them, it must name the package and pin an exact version. AGENTS.md requires that naming when a new Ratstack template package is added; the closer rule here is ADR 0008, which pins unstable dependencies.

**Revisit this if** a later release wants in-chat conversation (threads, "reply to answer", streaming). Then `chat` plus Cloudflare's `agents/chat-sdk` state adapter is the route to evaluate, and #295's exclusion of in-chat Answer submission would need its own ADR.

## 2. Answers to the issue's questions

| Question | Answer | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does `vercel/chat` run on Workers with Alchemy and Effect 4.1.x (`nodejs_compat`)? | Yes, mechanically. `wrangler deploy --dry-run` bundles Slack, Teams and both together, and local workerd serves and rejects bad signatures. It is promise-based, so every call is wrapped in `Effect.tryPromise`. No Alchemy-specific obstacle was found, but I did not deploy through Alchemy. | §2.1, *measured* |
| Workerd compatibility and footprint? | Slack full: 277 KiB gz. Teams full: 897 KiB gz, 1.8 s active startup in the one local profile that finished (two others timed out at 10 s). Both: 996 KiB gz. Stateless subpaths: 13 KiB gz. Worker size limit is 64 MiB, so **startup time, not size, is the limiter.** | §2.1, *measured* |
| Signature verification and stateless handling in `MainWorker`? | Slack: HMAC-SHA256 with Web Crypto, 5-minute skew, no state. Teams: Microsoft's JWT check, which the stateless subpath does **not** implement; we write it. | §3.2 |
| Does it need Redis or another external store? | The `Chat` constructor requires a `StateAdapter`; official ones are Redis, ioredis, Postgres, memory. Redis and Postgres are third-party stores and break SPEC §6. A DO SQLite `StateAdapter` exists but is Cloudflare's `agents/chat-sdk`, not part of `vercel/chat`. With thin adapters, **no `StateAdapter` is required.** | §3.3 |
| Card fidelity? | Slack Block Kit and Teams Adaptive Cards both carry what R3 needs: rating links, a Reminder, a Result summary, and later edits. Plain-link Invitations are possible on both. | §3.4 |
| Slack app and Teams bot registration and per-Organization OAuth install? | Slack: standard distributed app plus OAuth v2 install per workspace. Teams: Entra app plus Azure Bot plus Teams app package; per-tenant admin install; tenancy model unresolved. | §3.5, §3.6 |
| Teams proactive messages, and where does the conversation reference live? | Needs the bot installed in the Person's personal scope, plus tenant id, user id and service URL. Store the per-Person reference in the **Organization Durable Object**; D1 holds only the tenant-to-Organization routing row. | §3.6 |
| Safe Links and the fragment `#t=…&v=…`? | **Not tested.** Microsoft documents that Teams links are checked at click time and not rewritten, and says nothing about fragments. Teams is gated on the fragment surviving. Whether Microsoft receives it is a separate question a `location.hash` check cannot answer. | §3.7 |
| Slack plain links and `block_actions`? | Slack documents `block_actions` as the payload for Block Kit interactive components, and a URL button still sends one. Plain `<url\|text>` links in message text are not interactive components. **Slack does not state "plain links send nothing" in so many words;** the conclusion follows from its payload list and is a one-click live check. | §3.8 |

### 2.1 How the footprint was measured

In a scratch directory outside the repository I installed the four 4.45.0 packages (plus `@chat-adapter/state-memory`) and wrote five tiny Worker entries. Each used `compatibility_date = 2026-11-01` and `nodejs_compat`, wrangler 4.165.0, Node 26.

| Entry | `wrangler deploy --dry-run` | Local `wrangler check startup`, active CPU |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stateless subpaths only (`slack/webhook`, `slack/api`, `slack/blocks`, `teams/api`, `teams/cards`, `teams/webhook`) | 56.5 KiB / **13.1 KiB gz** | 19 / 99 / 59 ms |
| `Chat` + Slack adapter + memory state | 1,324 KiB / **277 KiB gz** | 232 / 93 / 63 ms |
| `Chat` + Teams adapter + memory state | 4,839 KiB / **897 KiB gz** | 1,795 ms; the other two runs timed out at 10 s |
| `Chat` + Slack + Teams + memory state | 5,332 KiB / **996 KiB gz** | 952 / 449 / 700 ms |
| For scale: Effect HttpApi Worker (`docs/research/effect-on-workers.md`) | about 86 KiB gz | 54–61 ms |

Caveats that matter:

- Startup numbers are **local workerd on a shared, noisy machine**, so they are indicative only. Cloudflare warns that production CPUs differ, and `docs/research/effect-on-workers.md` makes the same point. The Worker startup limit is 1 s ([Workers limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/)). A Teams adapter that sometimes needs more than a second locally is not a safe thing to load into `MainWorker`.
- The Worker size limit on both plans is 64 MiB (same page), so 1 MiB gzip is not a size problem. It is a startup-parse and review-surface problem.
- Behaviour check in local workerd: `bot.webhooks.slack` returned `401 Invalid signature` for a bad signature, and `bot.webhooks.teams` returned `401` for a missing `Authorization` header. That proves the modules load and the rejection path works. **It does not prove a valid inbound activity or an outbound send**, which need real Slack and Azure credentials.
- Why the Teams adapter is so heavy: its dependencies are `@microsoft/teams.apps` (needs Node ≥ 22.12; depends on `express`, `axios`, `jsonwebtoken`, `jwks-rsa`, `@azure/msal-node`, `@microsoft/signalr`, `reflect-metadata`) plus `teams.api`, `teams.cards`, `teams.graph` and `teams.graph-endpoints` ([npm metadata](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/teams.apps)). Slack's full adapter pulls `@slack/web-api` and `@slack/socket-mode`.

## 3. Evidence

### 3.1 What `vercel/chat` is

- Chat SDK is a TypeScript bot framework: a `Chat` instance holds platform adapters and one state adapter; handlers such as `bot.onNewMention` and `onSubscribedMessage` run for events from every adapter, and each adapter exposes `bot.webhooks.<name>` ([Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/chat-sdk/adapters)). Repository: [vercel/chat](https://github.com/vercel/chat), MIT.
- The state adapter "share[s] subscriptions, locks, and cached data across requests" (same page). Core `Chat` calls it on every inbound message: `setIfNotExists` for `dedupe:<adapter>:<messageId>` and `acquireLock` per thread (read in `chat@4.45.0` `dist/index.js`).
- Release cadence is fast: 4.38.0 on 2026-08-14 to 4.45.0 on 2026-11-13. The docs warn that protected members of official adapters "can change in minor releases, so pin the adapter version" ([Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/chat-sdk/adapters)).
- The repo already pins Effect and Alchemy together because both are unstable or beta (ADR 0008). A third fast-moving dependency in the send path is a cost, not a saving, for a surface of about five calls per platform.

where URLs are rewritten to `*.safelinks.protection.outlook.com` (the existing note `docs/research/email-link-scanners.md`).
- The Built-in protection preset applies Safe Links protection in Teams to every recipient in a tenant with at least one Defender for Office 365 licence.
- "The intermediary page that does Safe Links validation redirects to the target page", which the page mentions when explaining why `SameSite=Strict` cookies may fail after opening a link from Teams.

What it does not say: whether the validation request includes the fragment, whether the intermediary redirect keeps it, or whether links inside a bot's Adaptive Card are treated like links in a typed message. A browser inherits the original fragment across an HTTP 3xx redirect when the `Location` header carries none (RFC 9110 §10.2.2), but the page does not say the intermediary uses a 3xx rather than a script redirect.

Two separate risks follow:

If the fragment does not survive, the Teams Invitation has no anonymous-safe handoff to `answer.html`. The Channel ADR must treat that as **blocking for Teams**, not as a degraded mode.
2. **The fragment reaches Microsoft.** If the click-time check sends the full URL to Microsoft's service, the Invitation token (ADR 0005 keeps it in the fragment so that no scanner or log ever sees it) is exposed to a third party. Email already has the same unknown; this note adds no evidence either way.

Test plan for the spike: in a Defender-licensed test tenant with Teams protection on, post a bot Adaptive Card whose link is `https://<preview-stage>/a#t=TEST&v=3`; click it from desktop, web and mobile; read `location.hash` on the answer page (it can log nothing but its own hash to the console for the test). That a click sends nothing is the same inference from the payload list, not a sentence Slack publishes.
- The Events API `link_shared` event is sent "when a link — matching the registered URL domain your app is setup to track — is posted", not when it is clicked; it also requires a subscription and a registered domain, and apps do not receive it for their own messages ([link_shared](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/link_shared/)). SurveyBeat should register no unfurl domain and subscribe to no `link_shared`.
- **What is not stated.** Slack does not publish a sentence of the form "clicking a plain link sends nothing to the app". The conclusion rests on the payload list above. Unfurling is a separate matter: with `unfurl_links` left on, Slack's servers may fetch the URL (they send no fragment); set `unfurl_links` and `unfurl_media` to false as #295 requires. 1. **Port, not product.** `ChannelSender` stays in `packages/domain` with no Slack, Teams or Cloudflare imports; Slack and Teams senders live in `packages/cloudflare` (boundary rules, ADR 0008). The domain port speaks Invitation, Reminder and Result summary, not "message" or "thread".

SPEC §5.1 still says that in Slack and Teams the message has interactive buttons and, where the platform allows it, a modal, and §5.7 says members can answer from the messages. #295 and this constraint require plain links and no buttons. # Remote MCP Authentication and Streamable HTTP Transport on MainWorker

Research for [issue #301](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/301). Checked on 2026-11-20 against repo pins `better-auth@1.7.25`, `effect@4.1.4`, and `@alchemy.run/cloudflare@2.0.0-beta.87`, plus published npm tarballs for `@better-auth/mcp@1.7.25`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25`, `@better-auth/core@1.7.25`, `@better-auth/cimd@1.7.25`, `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@1.2.4`, and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.2`.

> [!NOTE]
> `node_modules` was not materialized on initial checkout, so Better Auth 1.7.25 and candidate package internals were verified directly from the published npm package tarballs for the exact repo pins and cross-checked against `packages/auth`, `packages/cloudflare`, `packages/domain`, and `docs/adr/`. `SPEC.md` and `docs/adr/` were not modified (issue #296 owns the `SPEC.md` release-order update).

## 1. Recommendation

1. **OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + Consent (`@better-auth/mcp@1.7.25`)**: Add **`@better-auth/mcp@1.7.25`** (which wraps **`@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25`**, plus **`@better-auth/cimd@1.7.25`** if Client ID Metadata Documents are enabled) to SurveyBeat's existing Better Auth configuration in `packages/auth` on D1.
   - Configure `mcp({ disableJwtPlugin: true, ... })` so access tokens are **opaque** (stored by hash in D1) rather than stateless JWTs, and validate `/mcp` Bearer tokens on `MainWorker` directly against D1 rather than relying solely on `@better-auth/mcp`'s `requireMcpAuth`.
   - Reject `@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@1.2.4`: it requires a dedicated Cloudflare KV namespace (`OAUTH_KV`), duplicating auth state outside D1 (violating SPEC §6.2's "Do not use [KV] for sessions that must be revoked at once" and ADR 0022's single-provider rule).
2. **MCP Server & Streamable HTTP Transport (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.2`)**: Serve `POST /mcp` on `MainWorker` using `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js` (`Server`) and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/webStandardStreamableHttp.js` (`WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport`) in **stateless per-request mode** (`sessionIdGenerator: undefined`, `enableJsonResponse: true`), initialized with `CfWorkerJsonSchemaValidator` (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/validation/cfworker`) and wrapped by a thin Effect adapter that generates tool JSON Schemas and validates tool inputs/outputs with **Effect Schema**.
   - Do **not** adopt `effect/ai/McpServer` (`effect@4.1.4`) yet: its stateless `McpServer.layerHttpRequestScoped` rejects every protocol older than `2026-07-28`, while its `2025-11-25`/`2025-03-26` `McpServer.layerHttp` stores `mcp-session-id` in an isolate-local `Map` and forks a background fiber.

---

## 2. Better Auth 1.7.25 Package Name & OAuth Comparison

### Confirmed Package Name at Pin `1.7.25`

Inspecting `better-auth@1.7.25` (`dist/plugins/index.d.mts`) confirms that **`better-auth/plugins` does not export an `mcp` plugin**. At `1.7.25`, Better Auth ships MCP support as separate scoped packages pinned alongside `better-auth`:

| Package (`1.7.25`) | Role at `1.7.25` | Key dependencies / exports |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `better-auth` (`1.7.25`) | Core auth, `emailOTP`, `magicLink`, `admin`, `organization`, `jwt` | No `mcp` export in `better-auth/plugins` |
| `@better-auth/mcp` (`1.7.25`) | **Real MCP plugin package**; wraps `oauthProvider` for RFC 9728 / RFC 8707 | Depends on `@better-auth/oauth-provider@^1.7.25`, `jose@^6.1.3`; exports `mcp`, `requireMcpAuth`, `createMcpProtectedRequestHandler` |
| `@better-auth/oauth-provider` (`1.7.25`) | Underlying OAuth 2.1 / OIDC Authorization Server plugin | Peer-depends on `better-auth@^1.7.25`, `@better-auth/core@^1.7.25`; exports `oauthProvider`, metadata helpers |

## 5. Storage Changes

### D1 (`packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/0011_better_auth_mcp.sql` + `d1-migrations.lock.json`)

D1 remains strictly the global auth/routing index—**no survey content** (no Pulses, Rounds, Submissions, Answers, Results, Themes, Actions, or Notes) is ever stored in D1.

With `disableJwtPlugin: true`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.25` needs six `auth_`-prefixed tables, plus one optional table (`auth_oauth_client_assertion`, only if CIMD `private_key_jwt` clients are enabled). Map them in `AUTH_TABLES` in `packages/auth/src/options.ts`. No `jwks` table is needed:

| Table | Purpose | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auth_oauth_client` | Registered MCP clients (CIMD/DCR/static) | `clientId` (unique), `redirectUris`, `scopes`, `tokenEndpointAuthMethod`, `requirePKCE`, `disabled`, `userId` |
| `auth_oauth_resource` | Canonical resource policies (`/mcp`) | `identifier` (unique), `allowedScopes`, `accessTokenTtl`, `refreshTokenTtl`, `disabled` |
| `auth_oauth_client_resource` | Client-to-resource allow mapping | `(clientId, resourceId)` unique pair with `ON DELETE CASCADE` |
| `auth_oauth_consent` | Active user-per-Organization grants | `(clientId, userId, referenceId)` where `referenceId` stores SurveyBeat `OrganizationId`; deleting this row revokes the grant |
| `auth_oauth_refresh_token` | Hashed refresh tokens (`offline_access`) | `token` (unique), `clientId`, `userId`, `sessionId` (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), `referenceId`, `scopes`, `resources`, `revoked`, `expiresAt` |
| `auth_oauth_access_token` | Hashed opaque access tokens | `token` (unique), `clientId`, `userId`, `sessionId` (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), `referenceId`, `refreshId`, `scopes`, `resources`, `confirmation` (reject a DPoP `jkt` on the Bearer path), `revoked`, `expiresAt` |
| `auth_oauth_client_assertion` | Optional `private_key_jwt` `jti` replay guard | Only needed if CIMD `private_key_jwt` clients are enabled (`id`, `expiresAt`) |

Note on D1 batching: `@effect/sql-d1` / Cloudflare D1 has no SQL `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` transactions (`docs/research/effect-on-workers.md`), so multi-table grant deletion uses `database.batch([...])`.

### Organization Durable Object

**Zero schema changes required.** The `Organization` DO remains the sole system of record for `person` (`auth_user_id`, `removed_at`, `organization_admin`), `membership` (`team_id`, `person_id`, `role`, `ended_at`), and all survey entities.

### Worker Configuration & Routing

- Add `"/mcp"` and `"/.well-known/*"` to `mainWorkerAssets.runWorkerFirst` in `packages/cloudflare/src/WorkerWiring.ts` and route them in `packages/cloudflare/src/MainWorker.ts` (`/.well-known/*` to `authInstance.fetch`, `/mcp` to the authenticated MCP handler).
- If `@better-auth/cimd` is enabled to fetch external client metadata URLs from `MainWorker`, ensure the `global_fetch_strictly_public` compatibility flag is configured in Alchemy for `MainWorker` (matching Cloudflare's CIMD SSRF guidance).
